_schema._about: Content for /work, rendered by tools/render_rights_work_book.py (CSS 44-work.css). Order: a black hero with the honest line and the real example ads as a static poster grid, the three contract commitments (static text, no count-up), hypjam's formats with illustrative sample hooks, the platforms we cut for, then the shared closing card (partials/page-cta.html). hypjam has no clients to show yet and invents none: no reserved slots, no quote wall, no invented brand names (SPEC §8 rank 2, §9). British English, sentence case, never 'studio'.
_schema.hero: {h1, h1_break_after, honest, cta:{label, href, micro}} - h1 wraps after h1_break_after on desktop. honest is the one-line disclosure under the heading and must stay while the grid shows example ads rather than client work. cta renders as a .cta-link text link (data-cta='work') under the grid, so the page never shows two filled booking buttons in one view.
_schema.ads: {label, list_label, items:[{id, format, credit, alt, play, video, poster}]} - the real example ads, poster only until pressed; pressing swaps the button for a <video controls> and pauses any other clip playing on the page (inline script in the renderer). Captions are the owner's own confirmed wording and mirror the homepage hero (content/hero.json → work): '@this_avi.ag, ex-Cluely' is Avi, the founder; 'Made for Cluely' is a real ad made for and run by Cluely; '@ajain_ugc, ex-Replit creator'. Posters are hook or opening frames with no third-party logo in them (the car film uses ugc-cinematic-urus-clean-poster.jpg, taken at 0.7s before the badge is legible; the screen demo must never use a frame from 0:03 on).
_schema.facts: {label, h2, p, cells:[{value, label}]} - the three contract clauses, worded exactly as home.json → process.commitments and the page-cta card. Static text; never animated, never results.
_schema.formats: {eyebrow, h2, intro, formats:[{id, name, blurb, tags}], samples_label, samples:[{category, format_id, hook, note, creator_brief, status}]} - hypjam's own formats. samples are illustrative hooks labelled by category ('A skincare brand'), never an invented brand name; status renders as a small chip on every tile.
_schema.platforms: {groups:[{label, tiles:[{id, text, render}]}]} - the platforms and placements we cut for, set typographically at 60% opacity with the sprite glyph on the first row. No third-party logo files.
_schema.cta: {h2, p, button:{label, href}} - feeds the shared closing card (partials/page-cta.html) through page meta cta-h2 / cta-p / cta-label / cta-href. p is the canonical call promise (SPEC §6.6).

formats.h2: UGC ads that sound like a creator, not a brand deck.
formats.intro: This is what ‘directed, not just sourced’ looks like on a feed: the formats we build, and sample hooks showing how a hook, a creator and a format come together. The samples are illustrative, written for the kinds of brand we make ads for. None of them is a client.

formats.name: Hooks and ads
formats.blurb: The first three seconds decide everything, so that is where we spend most of our energy. We script, cast and shoot scroll-stopping hooks built for feed placement, not just brand safety.

formats.name: Testimonials
formats.blurb: Creator-led reviews, scripted and directed, and run as ads. Creators only say what they have tried and what your claims can stand behind, and paid partnerships are labelled.

formats.name: Founder-led
formats.blurb: Sometimes the best spokesperson is the person who built the thing. We direct founders through the same process as the roster, hooks, retakes and all, so they do not have to wing it on camera.

formats.name: Trends and sounds
formats.blurb: We track what is actually moving on the app this week, not last quarter's trend report. Then we brief creators to bend it around your product instead of bolting your logo onto someone else's meme.

formats.name: Whitelisting
formats.blurb: Your best-performing organic content, running as paid from the creator's own handle. We handle the usage rights and the Spark Ads setup so the ad keeps the creator's credibility intact.

formats.name: Scripts and edits
formats.blurb: Every video starts as a proper script, not a vague vibe brief, and ends with an edit built for the platform it is going on. Same team end to end, so nothing gets lost in translation.
